content.overview: Section 19 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 regulates cognizance of offences under the Act. No court shall take cognizance of any offence except on a complaint made by the Central Government or any authority or officer authorised by the Central Government, or by any person who has given notice of not less than sixty days of the alleged offence and of the intention to make a complaint to the Central Government or the authorised officer/authority, as the section provides.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Complaint by Central Government/authorised officer? OR (2) Private complaint after 60-day notice? (3) Notice contents compliant? (4) Linked to s. 15 offence?
content.study:
s. 19 is a cognizance filter. Prosecution without the prescribed complaint route is barred. Private prosecution requires prior statutory notice.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Bar on cognizance
sections.body: No court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Act except as s. 19 provides.

sections.heading: Official complaint
sections.body: Complaint by the Central Government or any authority or officer authorised in that behalf.

sections.heading: Private complaint route
sections.body: Any person may complain after giving not less than sixty days' notice of the alleged offence and of intention to complain to the Central Government or authorised officer/authority — as enacted.

sections.heading: Link to s. 15
sections.body: Cognizance rules apply to offences whose penalty is framed under s. 15 and related provisions.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Check who filed the complaint and whether the 60-day notice path was used correctly if private.

examples.title: Private notice
examples.body: A resident gives 60 days' notice of an alleged s. 7/s. 15 contravention to the authorised authority and then files a complaint — s. 19 private route is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Can a court take cognizance on a police chargesheet alone under the EPA?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 19 requires complaint by the Central Government/authorised officer or by a person after statutory notice; the prescribed complaint route controls.

distinctions.title: s. 19 cognizance vs s. 15 penalty
distinctions.left: Who may trigger court cognizance and on what conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Anyone can file an EPA criminal complaint without notice.
misconceptions.correction: Private complaints require prior notice of not less than sixty days as s. 19 provides; official complaints need authorised complainant.
